Compute the features of a table

Source: R/feature-pipeline.R
compute_features.Rd

compute_features() evaluates a feature_pipeline() on data and returns a tsibble made of the key, the index, and the outputs of the nodes that apply. Raw columns that are only read by nodes are not carried into the feature table unless a node produces them.

Every node runs once, sees only its declared inputs, and its result is matched back on the key and index of data. Missing, duplicated or extra key/index rows all abort the computation, so a half-aligned feature table is never returned.

Usage

compute_features(.data, pipeline, stage = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_ts'
compute_features(.data, pipeline, stage = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
compute_features(.data, pipeline, stage = NULL, ...)

Arguments

.data

A tsibble.

pipeline

A feature_pipeline().

stage

NULL (default) runs every node in the pipeline. "history" runs the nodes that apply to the historical table, "future" those that apply to the future table.

...

Passed on to individual methods.

Value

A tsibble holding the key, the index and the pipeline outputs, with the column types, key/index metadata and grouping of .data.

See also

feature_forecast()

Examples

library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
tsbl <- tsibble(
  id = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 4), t = rep(1:4, 2),
  value = 1:8, key = id, index = t
)
lagged <- feature_node(
  "lagged", function(x) mutate(x, value_lag = lag(value)),
  outputs = "value_lag", inputs = "value"
)
compute_features(tsbl, feature_pipeline(lagged))
#> # A tsibble: 8 x 3 [1]
#> # Key:       id [2]
#>   id        t value_lag
#>   <chr> <int>     <int>
#> 1 a         1        NA
#> 2 a         2         1
#> 3 a         3         2
#> 4 a         4         3
#> 5 b         1        NA
#> 6 b         2         5
#> 7 b         3         6
#> 8 b         4         7
